topic: Quadratic and line with no intersection, integer parameter
problem: The graphs of y=x^2+4x+q and y=3x+10 have no points of intersection, where q is an integer. What is the least possible value of q?

bad.why: Needs the memorized condition b^2-4ac<0, collecting terms by hand, and solving an inequality; the slider shows the answer directly.
Checking the difference at a single x-value cannot show the graphs never meet.

algebraFirst.description: Sets the equations equal, rewrites x^2+x+(q-10)=0, requires the discriminant 1-4(q-10)<0, solves q>41/4, and rounds up to 11.

explanationNotes: Explain 'no points of intersection' as the parabola staying completely above the line. Dragging the whole-number slider q upward, the graphs still cross at q=10 and separate at q=11, so 11 is the least possible integer.
notes: Original variant of Bedrock Prep's hard '2 Quadratics with No Solution' and 'Lowest Possible Sum' categories. The difference is x^2+x+q-10 with minimum q-41/4; no intersection requires q>41/4, so least integer q is 11. A calculator method should make the integer q condition explicit and check the two full graphs, not a single x sample. Source category: https://www.bedrockprep.com/problems
